sanskrit: pralobhanārthaṃ tasyātha prāhiṇot pākaśāsanaḥ divyām apsarasaṃ puṇyāṃ darśanīyām alambusām
english: Then, to tempt him, the Chastiser of Pāka sent forth a celestial apsaras, holy and fair to behold, named Alambusā.

sanskrit: tasya tarpayato devān sarasvatyāṃ mahātmanaḥ samīpato mahārāja sopātiṣṭhata bhāminī
english: As that great-souled one was offering libations to the gods upon the Sarasvatī, O great king, the lovely woman drew near and stood close beside him.

sanskrit: tāṃ divyavapuṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasyarṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ retaḥ skannaṃ sarasvatyāṃ tat sā jagrāha nimnagā
english: Beholding her of celestial form, the seed of that contemplative sage spilled forth into the Sarasvatī, and the river took it up.

sanskrit: kukṣau cāpy adadhad dṛṣṭvā tad retaḥ puruṣarṣabha sā dadhāra ca taṃ garbhaṃ putrahetor mahānadī
english: Seeing that seed, O bull among men, she received it into her womb; and that great river bore the embryo for the sake of a son.

sanskrit: suṣuve cāpi samaye putraṃ sā saritāṃ varā jagāma putram ādāya tam ṛṣiṃ prati ca prabho
english: In due time that best of rivers gave birth to a son, and taking the child she went to that sage, O lord.

sanskrit: ṛṣisaṃsadi taṃ dṛṣṭvā sā nadī munisattamam tataḥ provāca rājendra dadatī putram asya tam brahmarṣe tava putro 'yaṃ tvadbhaktyā dhārito mayā
english: Seeing that most excellent of sages in the assembly of seers, the river, O lord of kings, spoke thus as she handed over his son: 'O brahmā-seer, this is your son, borne by me out of devotion to you.'

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā te 'psarasaṃ reto yat skannaṃ prāg alambusām tat kukṣiṇā vai brahmarṣe tvadbhaktyā dhṛtavaty aham
english: 'When at the sight of the apsaras Alambusā your seed was once spilled, that, O brahmā-seer, I held within my womb out of devotion to you.'

sanskrit: na vināśam idaṃ gacchet tvatteja iti niścayāt pratigṛhṇīṣva putraṃ svaṃ mayā dattam aninditam
english: 'Resolved that this radiance of yours should not perish, I bore it; receive now your own blameless son, given to you by me.'

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratijagrāha prītiṃ cāvāpa uttamām mantravac copajighrat taṃ mūrdhni premṇā dvijottamaḥ
english: Thus addressed, that best of twice-born accepted him and felt the highest delight; with mantras and with love he kissed the boy upon the head.

sanskrit: pariṣvajya ciraṃ kālaṃ tadā bharatasattama sarasvatyai varaṃ prādāt prīyamāṇo mahāmuniḥ
english: Embracing him a long while, O best of the Bharatas, the great sage, well pleased, then granted a boon to the Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: viśve devāḥ sapitaro gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ tṛptiṃ yāsyanti subhage tarpyamāṇās tavāmbhasā
english: 'The Viśvedevas together with the fathers, and the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases, shall attain satisfaction, O fortunate one, when honored with libations of your waters.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā sa tu tuṣṭāva vacobhir vai mahānadīm prītaḥ paramahṛṣṭātmā yathāvac chṛṇu pārthiva
english: Having spoken thus, pleased and supremely joyful in heart, he praised the great river with these words; hear them duly, O king.

sanskrit: prasṛtāsi mahābhāge saraso brahmaṇaḥ purā jānanti tvāṃ saricchreṣṭhe munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: 'O greatly blessed one, you flowed forth of old from the lake of Brahmā; the sages of strict vows know you, O best of rivers.'

sanskrit: mama priyakarī cāpi satataṃ priyadarśane tasmāt sārasvataḥ putro mahāṃs te varavarṇini
english: 'And you have ever done me kindness, O lovely to behold; therefore great shall be your son Sārasvata, O fair-complexioned one.'

sanskrit: tavaiva nāmnā prathitaḥ putras te lokabhāvanaḥ sārasvata iti khyāto bhaviṣyati mahātapāḥ
english: 'Renowned by your very name, your son, a benefactor of the worlds, shall become famed as Sārasvata, great in austerity.'

sanskrit: eṣa dvādaśavārṣikyām anāvṛṣṭyāṃ dvijarṣabhān sārasvato mahābhāge vedān adhyāpayiṣyati
english: 'During a drought of twelve years, O greatly blessed one, this Sārasvata shall teach the Vedas to the bulls among the twice-born.'

sanskrit: puṇyābhyaś ca saridbhyas tvaṃ sadā puṇyatamā śubhe bhaviṣyasi mahābhāge matprasādāt sarasvati
english: 'And of all holy rivers you shall ever be the most holy, O auspicious one, O greatly blessed Sarasvatī, by my grace.'

sanskrit: evaṃ sā saṃstutā tena varaṃ labdhvā mahānadī putram ādāya muditā jagāma bharatarṣabha
english: Thus praised by him, the great river, having received her boon, took her son and went away rejoicing, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu virodhe devadānavaiḥ śakraḥ praharaṇānveṣī lokāṃs trīn vicacāra ha
english: At that very time, in the strife between the gods and the dānavas, Śakra, seeking a weapon, ranged through the three worlds.

sanskrit: na copalebhe bhagavāñ śakraḥ praharaṇaṃ tadā yad vai teṣāṃ bhaved yogyaṃ vadhāya vibudhadviṣām
english: Yet the lord Śakra found then no weapon that would be fit to slay those foes of the gods.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt surāñ śakro na me śakyā mahāsurāḥ ṛte 'sthibhir dadhīcasya nihantuṃ tridaśadviṣaḥ
english: Then Śakra said to the gods: 'These mighty asuras, foes of the thirty, cannot be slain by me save with the bones of Dadhīca.'

sanskrit: tasmād gatvā ṛṣiśreṣṭho yācyatāṃ surasattamāḥ dadhīcāsthīni dehīti tair vadhiṣyāmahe ripūn
english: 'Therefore go, O best of gods, and let that foremost of sages be entreated: "Give the bones of Dadhīca"—with them we shall slay our enemies.'

sanskrit: sa devair yācito 'sthīni yatnād ṛṣivaras tadā prāṇatyāgaṃ kuruṣveti cakāraivāvicārayan sa lokān akṣayān prāpto devapriyakaras tadā
english: Earnestly entreated by the gods to give up his bones—to lay down his very life—that best of sages did so without a moment's hesitation; and having done the gods this kindness, he won then the imperishable worlds.

sanskrit: tasyāsthibhir atho śakraḥ saṃprahṛṣṭamanās tadā kārayām āsa divyāni nānāpraharaṇāny uta vajrāṇi cakrāṇi gadā gurudaṇḍāṃś ca puṣkalān
english: From his bones, then, Śakra, with greatly delighted heart, had fashioned divine weapons of many kinds—thunderbolts, discuses, maces, and ample heavy staves.

sanskrit: sa hi tīvreṇa tapasā saṃbhṛtaḥ paramarṣiṇā prajāpatisutenātha bhṛguṇā lokabhāvanaḥ
english: For he, the benefactor of the worlds, had been begotten through fierce austerity by the supreme sage Bhṛgu, son of Prajāpati.

sanskrit: atikāyaḥ sa tejasvī lokasāravinirmitaḥ jajñe śailaguruḥ prāṃśur mahimnā prathitaḥ prabhuḥ nityam udvijate cāsya tejasā pākaśāsanaḥ
english: Vast of body, full of splendor, fashioned from the essence of the worlds, he was born—heavy as a mountain, towering, renowned for his might, a lord; ever did the Chastiser of Pāka tremble at his radiance.

sanskrit: tena vajreṇa bhagavān mantrayuktena bhārata bhṛśaṃ krodhavisṛṣṭena brahmatejobhavena ca daityadānavavīrāṇāṃ jaghāna navatīr nava
english: With that thunderbolt, charged with mantras, O Bhārata, hurled in furious wrath and sprung from the power of brahman, the lord slew nine times ninety of the daitya and dānava heroes.

sanskrit: atha kāle vyatikrānte mahaty atibhayaṃkare anāvṛṣṭir anuprāptā rājan dvādaśavārṣikī
english: Then, when a long and most terrible span of time had passed, a drought of twelve years came on, O king.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ dvādaśavārṣikyām anāvṛṣṭyāṃ maharṣayaḥ vṛttyarthaṃ prādravan rājan kṣudhārtāḥ sarvatodiśam
english: In that twelve-year drought the great seers, afflicted by hunger, fled in every direction in search of livelihood, O king.

sanskrit: digbhyas tān pradrutān dṛṣṭvā muniḥ sārasvatas tadā gamanāya matiṃ cakre taṃ provāca sarasvatī
english: Seeing them scattered to the quarters, the sage Sārasvata then made up his mind to depart; but the Sarasvatī spoke to him.

sanskrit: na gantavyam itaḥ putra tavāhāram ahaṃ sadā dāsyāmi matsyapravarān uṣyatām iha bhārata
english: 'You must not go from here, my son; I shall always give you food—the choicest of fishes; dwell here, O Bhārata.'

sanskrit: ity uktas tarpayām āsa sa pitṝn devatās tathā āhāram akaron nityaṃ prāṇān vedāṃś ca dhārayan
english: Thus addressed, he made offering to the fathers and to the gods, took his food daily, and so preserved both his life and the Vedas.

sanskrit: atha tasyām atītāyām anāvṛṣṭyāṃ maharṣayaḥ anyonyaṃ paripapracchuḥ punaḥ svādhyāyakāraṇāt
english: Then, when that drought had passed, the great seers questioned one another concerning the recitation of their sacred study once more.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ kṣudhāparītānāṃ naṣṭā vedā vidhāvatām sarveṣām eva rājendra na kaś cit pratibhānavān
english: For all of them, gripped by hunger and wandering about, the Vedas had been lost, O lord of kings; not one of them had any recollection left.

sanskrit: atha kaś cid ṛṣis teṣāṃ sārasvatam upeyivān kurvāṇaṃ saṃśitātmānaṃ svādhyāyam ṛṣisattamam
english: Then a certain one of the seers came upon Sārasvata, that most excellent and disciplined of sages, engaged in his sacred recitation.

sanskrit: sa gatvācaṣṭa tebhyaś ca sārasvatam atiprabham svādhyāyam amaraprakhyaṃ kurvāṇaṃ vijane jane
english: Going back, he told them of the brilliant Sārasvata, godlike in his luster, performing his sacred recitation in a solitary place.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve samājagmus tatra rājan maharṣayaḥ sārasvataṃ muniśreṣṭham idam ūcuḥ samāgatāḥ
english: Then all the great seers gathered there, O king, and, assembled before Sārasvata, that best of sages, said this:

sanskrit: asmān adhyāpayasveti tān uvāca tato muniḥ śiṣyatvam upagacchadhvaṃ vidhivad bho mamety uta
english: 'Teach us,' they said; and the sage replied to them: 'Become my pupils duly, sirs, according to the rule.'

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd ṛṣigaṇo bālas tvam asi putraka sa tān āha na me dharmo naśyed iti punar munīn
english: Then the company of seers said: 'You are but a boy, dear child.' He answered the sages again: 'So that my dharma not be lost.'

sanskrit: yo hy adharmeṇa vibrūyād gṛhṇīyād vāpy adharmataḥ mriyatāṃ tāv ubhau kṣipraṃ syātāṃ vā vairiṇāv ubhau
english: 'He who teaches against right, or who receives teaching against right—let both of them swiftly perish, or both become foes to each other.'

sanskrit: na hāyanair na palitair na vittena na bandhubhiḥ ṛṣayaś cakrire dharmaṃ yo 'nūcānaḥ sa no mahān
english: 'Not by years, nor by grey hairs, nor by wealth, nor by kinsmen did the seers determine eminence in dharma: he who is learned in the sacred lore is great among us.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā vacas tasya munayas te vidhānataḥ tasmād vedān anuprāpya punar dharmaṃ pracakrire
english: Hearing these words of his, those sages duly received the Vedas from him and re-established their dharma anew.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭir munisahasrāṇi śiṣyatvaṃ pratipedire sārasvatasya viprarṣer vedasvādhyāyakāraṇāt
english: Sixty thousand sages became the pupils of the brahmā-seer Sārasvata for the sake of recovering the recitation of the Vedas.

sanskrit: muṣṭiṃ muṣṭiṃ tataḥ sarve darbhāṇāṃ te 'bhyupāharan tasyāsanārthaṃ viprarṣer bālasyāpi vaśe sthitāḥ
english: Then each of them brought handful upon handful of darbha grass for the seat of that brahmā-seer; though he was but a boy, they remained obedient to him.

sanskrit: tatrāpi dattvā vasu rauhiṇeyo; mahābalaḥ keśavapūrvajo 'tha jagāma tīrthaṃ muditaḥ krameṇa; khyātaṃ mahad vṛddhakanyā sma yatra
english: There too the son of Rohiṇī, the mighty elder brother of Keśava, having bestowed wealth, then went on rejoicing, in due course, to that great and famed sacred ford where the Aged Maiden once dwelt.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ kumārī bhagavaṃs tapoyuktā hy abhūt purā kimarthaṃ ca tapas tepe ko vāsyā niyamo 'bhavat
english: Janamejaya said: How, O reverend one, did that maiden of old come to be devoted to austerity? For what purpose did she practice penance, and what was her vow?

sanskrit: suduṣkaram idaṃ brahmaṃs tvattaḥ śrutam anuttamam ākhyāhi tattvam akhilaṃ yathā tapasi sā sthitā
english: Most arduous and unsurpassed is this that I have heard from you, O brāhmaṇa; tell me the whole truth, how she stood firm in austerity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ṛṣir āsīn mahāvīryaḥ kuṇir gārgyo mahāyaśāḥ sa taptvā vipulaṃ rājaṃs tapo vai tapatāṃ varaḥ mānasīṃ sa sutāṃ subhrūṃ samutpāditavān vibhuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There was a sage of great vigor and great fame, Kuṇi of the line of Garga; having performed vast austerity, O king, that best of ascetics, the mighty one, brought forth from his mind a fair-browed daughter.

sanskrit: tāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā bhṛśaṃ prītaḥ kuṇir gārgyo mahāyaśāḥ jagāma tridivaṃ rājan saṃtyajyeha kalevaram
english: And beholding her, Kuṇi of Garga's line, of great fame, was exceedingly pleased; then, O king, casting off his body here, he went to heaven.

sanskrit: subhrūḥ sā hy atha kalyāṇī puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇā mahatā tapasogreṇa kṛtvāśramam aninditā
english: That fair-browed and lovely maiden, blameless, with eyes like lotus-petals, having built a hermitage, gave herself to fierce and mighty austerity.

sanskrit: upavāsaiḥ pūjayantī pitṝn devāṃś ca sā purā tasyās tu tapasogreṇa mahān kālo 'tyagān nṛpa
english: Honoring with fasts the fathers and the gods of old, she passed a great span of time in fierce austerity, O king.

sanskrit: sā pitrā dīyamānāpi bhartre naicchad aninditā ātmanaḥ sadṛśaṃ sā tu bhartāraṃ nānvapaśyata
english: Though offered by her father to a husband, that blameless one would not consent, for she saw no husband worthy of herself.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā tapasogreṇa pīḍayitvātmanas tanum pitṛdevārcanaratā babhūva vijane vane
english: Then, mortifying her own body with fierce austerity, she remained intent upon the worship of the fathers and the gods in a solitary forest.

sanskrit: sātmānaṃ manyamānāpi kṛtakṛtyaṃ śramānvitā vārddhakena ca rājendra tapasā caiva karśitā
english: Though she deemed herself to have fulfilled her purpose, she grew worn with toil, O lord of kings, wasted by old age and by penance alike.

sanskrit: sā nāśakad yadā gantuṃ padāt padam api svayam cakāra gamane buddhiṃ paralokāya vai tadā
english: When she could no longer walk even a single step by herself, she then set her mind upon passing to the other world.

sanskrit: moktukāmāṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā śarīraṃ nārado 'bravīt asaṃskṛtāyāḥ kanyāyāḥ kuto lokās tavānaghe
english: But seeing her wishing to release her body, Nārada said: 'Whence are there worlds for you, O sinless maiden, when you are unconsecrated by marriage?'

sanskrit: evaṃ hi śrutam asmābhir devaloke mahāvrate tapaḥ paramakaṃ prāptaṃ na tu lokās tvayā jitāḥ
english: 'For thus have we heard in the world of the gods, O woman of great vows: supreme austerity you have attained, but the worlds you have not won.'

sanskrit: tan nāradavacaḥ śrutvā sābravīd ṛṣisaṃsadi tapaso 'rdhaṃ prayacchāmi pāṇigrāhasya sattamāḥ
english: Hearing those words of Nārada, she said in the assembly of seers: 'I will give half of my austerity to him who takes my hand, O most excellent ones.'

sanskrit: ity ukte cāsyā jagrāha pāṇiṃ gālavasaṃbhavaḥ ṛṣiḥ prāk śṛṅgavān nāma samayaṃ cedam abravīt
english: When she had thus spoken, a sage sprung from Gālava, named Śṛṅgavān, took her hand and laid down this condition:

sanskrit: samayena tavādyāhaṃ pāṇiṃ sprakṣyāmi śobhane yady ekarātraṃ vastavyaṃ tvayā saha mayeti ha
english: 'On this condition shall I touch your hand today, O fair one: that you must dwell with me for a single night.'

sanskrit: tatheti sā pratiśrutya tasmai pāṇiṃ dadau tadā cakre ca pāṇigrahaṇaṃ tasyodvāhaṃ ca gālaviḥ
english: 'So be it,' she promised, and gave her hand to him then; and the son of Gālava took her hand and wedded her.

sanskrit: sā rātrāv abhavad rājaṃs taruṇī devavarṇinī divyābharaṇavastrā ca divyasraganulepanā
english: In the night she became, O king, a young woman of godlike complexion, adorned with celestial ornaments and raiment, with celestial garlands and unguents.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā gālaviḥ prīto dīpayantīm ivātmanā uvāsa ca kṣapām ekāṃ prabhāte sābravīc ca tam
english: Beholding her, who seemed to shine with her own radiance, the son of Gālava was delighted, and dwelt with her one night; at dawn she said to him:

sanskrit: yas tvayā samayo vipra kṛto me tapatāṃ vara tenoṣitāsmi bhadraṃ te svasti te 'stu vrajāmy aham
english: 'The condition you made with me, O brāhmaṇa, best of ascetics—by it I have dwelt with you; blessings upon you, may all be well with you; now I depart.'

sanskrit: sānujñātābravīd bhūyo yo 'smiṃs tīrthe samāhitaḥ vatsyate rajanīm ekāṃ tarpayitvā divaukasaḥ
english: Granted leave, she spoke once more: 'Whoever, intent in spirit, shall dwell one night at this ford, having made offering to the dwellers of heaven—'

sanskrit: catvāriṃśatam aṣṭau ca dve cāṣṭau samyag ācaret yo brahmacaryaṃ varṣāṇi phalaṃ tasya labheta saḥ evam uktvā tataḥ sādhvī dehaṃ tyaktvā divaṃ gatā
english: '—he shall obtain the fruit of one who duly observes chastity for eight-and-forty and for two-and-eight years.' Having spoken thus, the virtuous woman then cast off her body and went to heaven.

sanskrit: ṛṣir apy abhavad dīnas tasyā rūpaṃ vicintayan samayena tapo 'rdhaṃ ca kṛcchrāt pratigṛhītavān
english: The sage too grew downcast, brooding on her beauty; and by the terms of the pact he had with difficulty received half her austerity.

sanskrit: sādhayitvā tadātmānaṃ tasyāḥ sa gatim anvayāt duḥkhito bharataśreṣṭha tasyā rūpabalātkṛtaḥ etat te vṛddhakanyāyā vyākhyātaṃ caritaṃ mahat
english: Then, having perfected himself, he followed in her course, grief-stricken, O best of the Bharatas, overpowered by her beauty. This great tale of the Aged Maiden has now been told to you.

sanskrit: tatrasthaś cāpi śuśrāva hataṃ śalyaṃ halāyudhaḥ tatrāpi dattvā dānāni dvijātibhyaḥ paraṃtapa śuśoca śalyaṃ saṃgrāme nihataṃ pāṇḍavais tadā
english: While he abode there, the Plough-armed one heard that Śalya had been slain; and there too, having bestowed gifts upon the twice-born, O scorcher of foes, he grieved for Śalya, then slain in battle by the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: samantapañcakadvārāt tato niṣkramya mādhavaḥ papraccharṣigaṇān rāmaḥ kurukṣetrasya yat phalam
english: Then, passing out from the gate of Samantapañcaka, Rāma the Mādhava asked the company of seers what was the fruit of Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: te pṛṣṭā yadusiṃhena kurukṣetraphalaṃ vibho samācakhyur mahātmānas tasmai sarvaṃ yathātatham
english: Questioned by the lion of the Yadus about the fruit of Kurukṣetra, O lord, those great-souled ones recounted it all to him exactly as it was.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ prajāpater uttaravedir ucyate; sanātanā rāma samantapañcakam samījire yatra purā divaukaso; vareṇa satreṇa mahāvarapradāḥ
english: The seers said: Samantapañcaka is called, O Rāma, the eternal northern altar of Prajāpati, where of old the gods of heaven, the great bestowers of boons, worshipped with an excellent sacrifice.

sanskrit: purā ca rājarṣivareṇa dhīmatā; bahūni varṣāṇy amitena tejasā prakṛṣṭam etat kuruṇā mahātmanā; tataḥ kurukṣetram itīha paprathe
english: And of old this field was ploughed through many years by the wise and best of royal seers, the great-souled Kuru of measureless splendor; thence it became famed in the world as Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: rāma uvāca kimarthaṃ kuruṇā kṛṣṭaṃ kṣetram etan mahātmanā etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ kathyamānaṃ tapodhanāḥ
english: Rāma said: For what purpose was this field ploughed by the great-souled Kuru? This I wish to hear told, O you whose wealth is austerity.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ purā kila kuruṃ rāma kṛṣantaṃ satatotthitam abhyetya śakras tridivāt paryapṛcchata kāraṇam
english: The seers said: Of old, O Rāma, as Kuru was ploughing, ever unwearied, Śakra came down from heaven, approached him, and asked the reason.

sanskrit: kim idaṃ vartate rājan prayatnena pareṇa ca rājarṣe kim abhipretaṃ yeneyaṃ kṛṣyate kṣitiḥ
english: 'What is this you are about, O king, with such utmost effort? O royal seer, what is your aim, that you plough this earth?'

sanskrit: kurur uvāca iha ye puruṣāḥ kṣetre mariṣyanti śatakrato te gamiṣyanti sukṛtāṃl lokān pāpavivarjitān
english: Kuru said: 'Those men who die upon this field, O Hundred-Sacrificer, shall go to the worlds of the virtuous, free from all sin.'

sanskrit: avahasya tataḥ śakro jagāma tridivaṃ prabhuḥ rājarṣir apy anirviṇṇaḥ karṣaty eva vasuṃdharām
english: Then, laughing in derision, the lord Śakra went back to heaven; but the royal seer, undaunted, kept on ploughing the earth.

sanskrit: āgamyāgamya caivainaṃ bhūyo bhūyo 'vahasya ca śatakratur anirviṇṇaṃ pṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭvā jagāma ha
english: Coming again and again, and mocking him again and again, the Hundred-Sacrificer, questioning him over and over, would each time depart, while Kuru remained undaunted.

sanskrit: yadā tu tapasogreṇa cakarṣa vasudhāṃ nṛpaḥ tataḥ śakro 'bravīd devān rājarṣer yac cikīrṣitam
english: But when the king ploughed the earth with fierce austerity, then Śakra told the gods what the royal seer was minded to do.
